name: American Healthcare REIT, Inc.
share_adj_basis: applied to revenue components only (v5.4); OE/share CAGR enters unadjusted

overrides_applied.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-27, accession 0001193125-26-082692), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Developments and capital expenditures': $(99,791) thousand for FY2023, $(91,940) thousand for FY2024 and $(128,562) thousand for FY2025; the override value is the median of the three filed years (the FY2023 figure). The same 10-K (Note 3, Real Estate Investments) reports capital expenditures incurred by segment of $100,971k / $87,562k / $143,103k for FY2023/24/25; the cash-flow line is used because the engine's capex is a cash concept.
overrides_applied.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 under every candidate tag the engine reads, because AHR reports its real-estate capex only as the combined cash-flow line 'Developments and capital expenditures' (ISHC development/expansion plus recurring property capex), which no engine candidate tag carries; the small PaymentsToAcquireOtherPropertyPlantAndEquipment series the engine does read ends at FY2020. The engine applies this single value to every missing period; it is the median of the three filed years. Against the true per-year figures it overstates FY2024 capex by $7,851,000 (conservative direction — lowers that year's OE) and understates FY2025 capex by $28,771,000 (flatters the latest year; noted, not hidden — the TTM pin used for the base charges the same $99,791,000 against TTM OCF, below FY2025's filed $128,562,000 run rate, so the base is if anything generous on capex). 'Acquisitions of real estate investments' ($884,425,000 in FY2025, same statement) is excluded: it is property M&A presented separately by the filer, not capex.
